zh_cn/壬戌[1]: Your strength is principle combined with flexibility. 魁罡 is a principled pillar, but water is fluid. So you keep your principle while being very soft in how you carry it through. People don't feel run over by your values, and yet they end up moving in the direction you were flowing toward.
zh_cn/壬辰[1]: Your strength is seeing the big picture. You sketch the large frame before the small tactics, and inside it you arrange people and resources. In the decisive moment, while everyone else is shaking, you quietly hold the center. That's the real power of 壬辰 — quiet most of the time, moving the world when it counts.
zh_cn/己丑[1]: Your strength is the instinct to save. 己丑 is soil that buries seeds. You don't spend money, emotion, trust, or time carelessly. You hold them for the right moment and then release them with precision. That's why you're stronger in a crisis than most people. When everyone else is empty, your storehouse still has something in it.
zh_cn/己丑[2]: Your shadow is staying frozen too long. 己丑 stores spring, but if you never open the storehouse, the soil itself hardens. If you don't let out what you've been holding, people can't read your heart even when they're standing next to you. 'Always fine' gets written on you, and beneath that label your private fatigue quietly stacks up.
zh_cn/己亥[1]: Your strength is flexible execution. 己亥 has the stability of earth and the fluidity of water at once. You can be planned and improvisational, principled and able to change direction when the situation calls for it. You survive in almost any environment.
zh_cn/己巳[2]: Your shadow is warmth that consumes you. 火生土 is beautiful as a structure — but fire feeds earth and uses itself up in the process. You look after people until one day you find yourself completely empty, and the people around you don't understand why you suddenly went distant. You don't even have the energy to explain.
zh_cn/己酉[2]: Your shadow is perfectionism. The precision of 己酉 is beautiful, but pushed too far it starts to close in on you. Hours on a detail no one will notice. Long disappointment over results that weren't quite right. And you apply the same standard to other people, which can hurt them without meaning to. Your bar is natural to you — but to others it can be a wall.
zh_cn/庚戌[0]: You share the 魁罡 (Commander) pillar with Geng-Jin — but where Geng-Jin sits on wet earth, you sit on dry. So your strength is drier, more decisive, more principled. You don't waver. But you don't bend either.
zh_cn/庚戌[2]: Your shadow is forgetting the sheath. 戌 (Xu) is the storage of fire — there's a hot interior inside that dry earth. If that heat isn't governed, your firmness can suddenly erupt as anger. And your standard, held too tightly, becomes an impossibly high wall to the people around you.
zh_cn/庚申[0]: You're the purest form of Geng. Geng-Shin is Geng sitting on its own 祿 (Lu) — double metal, layered on itself. So your standard doesn't shift, your judgment is clean, and your stance is steel. Not because you're trying to be — because that's the shape you were made in.
zh_cn/庚辰[0]: Your power doesn't announce itself. You can look unremarkable at a glance, and then at one decisive moment your weight shows. People say later, 'Wait — that person was that person?' In classical Saju, Geng-Jin is one of the four 魁罡 (Commander) pillars — among the strongest in the system.
zh_cn/戊戌[1]: The tradition names this pillar 魁罡, one of the four Commanders. Your strength is structural: an internal standard you don't trade away. When things get ugly, you're the person others rely on not to bend. Your steadiness is not performed — it's the actual shape of you.
zh_cn/戊辰[1]: Your strength is stored potential. 辰 holds water and wood inside dry earth — an aquifer under a plain. You are a long-game player: patient, quiet, arranging things until the moment it matters, and then moving with a weight that surprises everyone including people who thought they knew you.
zh_cn/甲辰[1]: Your strength is seeing the big picture. You sketch the large frame first and arrange people and resources inside it. And you don't rush. You grow heavily, slowly. That's the real strength of 甲辰 — quiet most of the time, moving the world when it counts.
zh_cn/甲辰[2]: Your shadow is holding the potential without releasing it. If 甲 doesn't use the water in 辰, it just stays pooled in the ground. Same for you. If you sketch a big picture but never bring it out, people don't know your potential. And over time the label 'what does that person actually do?' starts to attach.
zh_cn/癸巳[1]: Your strength is combining feeling with practicality. 癸 is sensitivity, 巳 is practical execution. You can feel something and put it into real action. People find you warm and precise at once. That combination is rare.
zh_cn/癸酉[1]: Your strength is refined wisdom. 癸's sensitivity meeting 酉's precision makes very sharp, very delicate insight. You read people's hearts accurately, and you name what they need. This is a rare gift. Your advice always hits a true spot.
zh_cn/癸酉[3]: 成熟的“Gye-You”能够驾驭这种敏锐性。既保持敏锐，又加以调整，以免耗尽自己的精力。这样一来，你的精准就不再是压力，而是成为人们慕名而来的那种深刻洞察力。
es/丁酉[3]: Un Ding-You maduro aplica sus criterios con generosidad. Tus criterios son un regalo, pero comprueba si la otra persona está preparada para recibirlo. Mantén tus criterios, pero no alejes a quienes tropiezan en el camino hacia ellos. Es entonces cuando tu calidez brilla de verdad.
es/乙酉[3]: Un Yi-You maduro aplica los cánones con generosidad. Conserva la belleza y comprende a quienes aún no pueden alcanzarla. Entonces, tu refinamiento deja de ser una presión y se convierte en el tipo de belleza que la gente quiere aprender.
es/己酉[3]: Un Ji-You maduro aplica la norma con generosidad. Mantiene el nivel de calidad, pero comprende a quienes aún no pueden alcanzarlo. Entonces, tu precisión deja de ser una presión y se convierte en ese tipo de belleza que la gente quiere aprender.
es/癸酉[3]: Un Gye-You maduro controla la sensibilidad. Mantiene la agudeza y la ajusta para que no te agote. Así, tu precisión deja de ser una presión y se convierte en ese tipo de comprensión profunda por la que la gente acude a ti.
es/辛酉[3]: Un Xin-You maduro comparte la perfección. Mantiene el nivel sin dejar de comprender a las personas que recorren el camino hacia ella. Entonces, tu perfección deja de ser una presión y se convierte en ese tipo de belleza que la gente quiere aprender.
